narrative.overview:
The link is the claim under review, and the page reports on it the way a careful fact-check does: a plain question, a rated answer, every source named, with no newspaper props. Serif tells the story (Newsreader, two static cuts), the system sans runs the interface, the system mono carries the link. Light is a cool, crisp near-white sheet with blue-black ink; dark is a deep cool ground with warm paper ink. Buttons are ink; one editor's blue marks only links, focus, the caret, and selection. Verdict hues appear only where a verdict is stated.

One 71rem column: the question 'Is this link what it says it is?', one supporting line, and the form; then the squared verdict band under its heavy rule (the registered domain in the serif under the verdict word), the link taken apart, the Evidence (the numbered strip as its index, then five questions on a rail or the eight Full rows), the actions, and history.

**Provenance.** Chosen 2026-10-24 by the owner after a 16-draft blind bake-off: P09 editorial as the base, P11's registered-domain line, P09's link taken apart and numbered citations, layer 2B's HTTPS question set; the headline is the one copy change.
keyCharacteristics: One 71rem column; form, history, and batch at 47.5rem; answers at 44rem.
Newsreader for the story; system sans for the interface; system mono for the link and data.
A squared verdict band, the only tinted container, under a heavy rule that draws when the verdict lands.
The registered domain in the serif directly under the verdict word.
Ink buttons; the accent never fills a control.
The strip's cells numbered 1-8 and cited by every Summary answer.
Shape before hue in the strip; found-nothing is a gray dash.
rules: The Danger Is Not a Verdict Rule
dos: Keep the order headline, form, band, the link taken apart, Evidence, actions, history.
State each fact once; the band only names the domain, the anatomy says the sentence.
Cite checks by the strip's numbers, with names alongside and names alone for assistive technology.
donts: No newspaper costume: mastheads, columns, datelines, small caps, newsprint.
No rounded band, no second tinted container.
No third font cut or face.
